The PSO example: a duplication and the two SNVs inside it, whose ordinals 1-5 occur exactly once each and give one traversal of the derivative chromosome. Ordinal 1 is the ALT G at chr1:20, 2 the REF at chr1:30, 3 the duplication junction, 4 the REF at chr1:20 and 5 the ALT T at chr1:30. The PSL table of the same subsection is excluded as an oracle (allele indices beyond the ALT list, inconsistent ploidy), and PSQ has no worked example in either version, so phase-set quality stays untested.

Two loci from this version's tandem-repeat subsection: the worked CNV:TR example (chr1:100, RN=1,3) with its two phased non-symbolic records, and the Figure 11 locus (chr1:200, RN=2,1) with the reviewer's correction that CAGCAGCAGTTGTTG is (CAG)3(TTG)2, giving RUS=CAG,TTG,CA, RUL=3,3,2, RUC=3,2,3 and RB=9,6,6. The specification's own rows omit the INFO column for the two non-symbolic records; '.' is supplied here. RN partitions the flattened lists differently on the two loci (1,3 and 2,1), so an implementation that ignored RN could not answer both.

The three assembly-contig insertions of the Large Insertions subsection: the complete insertion of <ctg1> (endpoints 1 and 329), the partial insertion of 7-214, and the circular insertion continuing from 229 past 329 to 1 and on to 45. All three reuse POS 123456/123457 and the IDs bnd_U/bnd_V in the specification, so the second and third are placed at distinct positions with distinct IDs and grouped by EVENT instead. Following the review, the printed MATEIDs are not registered as expected answers: on the chromosome-13 breakends the true mate is a contig-side breakend that has no record (two of the printed values are self-references and one names an undefined bnd_C), so only the circular pair bnd_X/bnd_Y, whose mates do have records, carries MATEID. The complete-insertion shorthand row is not included: '13 321682 INS0 T C<ctg1>' takes its POS and REF from an unrelated chr2 breakend, and the reviewer's corrected reading '13 123456 INS0 C C<ctg1>' is not spec-verbatim.

The four Number=M examples of the FORMAT-field subsection, verbatim. Their value counts were enumerated independently from the cardinality rules before being registered: 1 for chr:10 (the ALT A carries no C on either strand), 3 for chr:20 (the REF C, then the forward C and the reverse-strand C opposite the G of CTAG), 2 for chr:30 (both phased copies of the C, for each of the two chemistries) and 5 for the partially phased octoploid at chr:40, where the unphased G, A and C values aggregate at their first occurrence and the symbolic-free but irrelevant A alleles contribute none. The last value of chr:40 is missing, so that slot carries a base modification with no rate.

Reviewer-authored records, not spec-verbatim: the specification names the key families M[0-9]+[ACGTUN], DPM[0-9]+[ACGTUN] and ADM[0-9]+[ACGTUN] and their aliases but prints no record combining them. chr:50 carries M5mC beside its numeric form M27551C, which must denote the same modification, the DPM and ADM depths of that same modification, and M999999C, a numerically valid identifier no reader is expected to recognise. chr:60 carries MXaoN, whose base letter N means both strands of every base are reported with the negative strand immediately after the positive one. MXaoN with a capital X is the reserved spelling; the four prose occurrences of MxaoN are typos.

The four local-allele rows of the equivalence table, which the registered features-v4.5.vcf case cannot replace: there LAA=1,2 on a two-ALT record makes the local-to-global map the identity, so it cannot tell a correct implementation from one that ignores LAA. Here LAA=2,4 skips ALT alleles A and T, so local position 1 is global allele 2 and local position 2 is global allele 4. GT reads 2/2, not the printed 2/4: GT is Number=1 and not a local-allele field, and both LPL and the row's global PL are minimal at C/C. Row 4 carries an empty LAA, a REF-only site with one local allele.

The registered R29 case reads the fraction and the total detecting depth only, leaving ADM5mC in the fixture but never queried. This case separates all three quantities of the same modification of the same sample: 90 percent of the reads at the modification, 20 reads able to detect it and 18 carrying it.

Reviewer-authored, not spec-verbatim. The specification's PSL table is unusable as printed - GT=|1/2|3 uses an allele index beyond the ALT list, GT=1|2 does the same and its omitted leading indicator makes the first allele implicitly phased against its own PSL, and the two chr20 rows disagree on ploidy (reported as samtools/hts-specs#871). The reviewer's corrected rows are used instead: GT=|1/2|2 and GT=/0|1/0, both with in-range indices, explicit leading indicators and consistent ploidy. PSQ values are added by the reviewer, the specification defining PSQ at VCFv4.5.tex:808-809 without a worked example. The oracle: each PSQ value corresponds positionally to a PSL name, so at chr20:10 the first allele is chr20*10*1 with quality 40, the second is unphased with both values missing, and the third is chr19*5*1 with quality 30 - a phase-set name reused from another chromosome.

Reviewer-authored, not spec-verbatim: the rule is normative at VCFv4.5.tex:775-776 - a sample-genotype must not have values for both PS and PSL, and the two are not interoperable because PS is not connected to a specific haplotype - but the specification prints no worked example of it. Two samples describe the same pair of phased haplotypes in one record, SAMPLE1 through PS and SAMPLE2 through PSL, with the unused mechanism written as '.'. The oracle: PS attaches to the genotype as a whole and the GT order determines the haplotypes, while PSL names a phase set per allele value, so the first allele of each genotype is chr1*100*1 and the second chr1*100*2. Both samples must yield haplotype 1 = A,T and haplotype 2 = G,C, and neither may expose the mechanism it does not use.

The equivalence table at VCFv4.5.tex:703-710 writes each of four sites twice, once with LAA/LAD/LPL and once with the global AD/PL, and both rows of a pair encode the same information. The fixture carries both representations of all four sites, with GT corrected to 2/2 in the first local row (GT is Number=1 and not a local-allele field; the global row of the same pair prints 2/2). A Number=LR depth is indexed by the local allele set and a Number=R depth by the full ALT list, so the eighteen expected rows agree only if the local indices are resolved to global alleles: at POS 1 LAA=2,4 puts the local depths 20, 30 and 10 on global alleles 0, 2 and 4, exactly where the global AD=20,.,30,.,10 carries them, and the global vector holds the missing value at 1 and 3. POS 4 is the REF-only case, an empty LAA giving one local depth against AD=30,.,.,. The LPL-to-PL genotype correspondence is not tested: both sides expose only a positional genotype index, and nothing in the graph relates a genotype index to the allele pair it stands for, so recovering it would mean the query supplying the mapping rather than reading it.
